sections.title: Subject
sections.guidance: Pick the central subject of the image. One clear focal entity (a person, a creature, an object, an architectural piece) that the rest of the prompt will revolve around.
examples: A solitary lighthouse keeper in oilskin
A mechanical fox made of brass gears
A ruined cathedral overtaken by ivy

sections.title: Scenery
sections.guidance: Where is the subject? Describe the surrounding environment, setting, or backdrop. Concrete and visual; avoid abstract concepts here.
examples: Standing at the edge of a storm-lashed cliff
In a misty pine forest at dawn

sections.title: Lighting
sections.guidance: Define the light source, time of day, and mood of illumination. This is one of the strongest levers for visual impact.
examples: Golden hour with long warm shadows
Cold blue moonlight through broken glass
Volumetric god rays piercing dust-filled air

sections.title: Mood
sections.guidance: Emotional tone and atmosphere. How should the viewer feel? Use evocative but visual descriptors (melancholic, serene, ominous, triumphant).
examples: Tense and ominous, on the edge of violence

sections.title: Style
sections.guidance: Artistic style or medium reference. This anchors the visual language - photographic, painterly, illustrative, or genre-specific.
examples: Dark fantasy oil painting in the style of 19th century romanticism
